question: What is the product of UV radiations acting on oxygen molecules at higher levels of the atmosphere?
solution:
The correct answer is** '__Ozone__'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere is a product of** UV radiation acting on oxygen O2** molecules. O₂ is an O molecule that is a reactive agent.

 
 
• O₂ → O+O
 
• O+O₂ → O₃ (Ozone)
 
 
 
• The sun propagates ultraviolet radiation which has an adverse effect on living beings.
 
• This layer absorbs the radiations and prohibits them from entering the outer surface of the earth. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons:**

 
 
• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are nontoxic, nonflammable chemicals **containing atoms of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine**.
 
• They are used in the manufacture of **aerosol sprays, blowing agents for foams and packing materials, as solvents, and as refrigerants**.
 
• Chlorofluorocarbons are the **ozone-depleting substances** released from refrigerators and air conditioners.
 
• The (CFCs) produce “**active Chlorine” (Cl and ClO radicals) in the presence of UVradiations**, which react with ozone and destroy ozone catalytically by converting it into oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Water:**
 
 
• Water is an inorganic compound with the **chemical formula H₂O**.
 
• It is a transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance,
 
• Climate change affects the world's water in complex ways. From unpredictable rainfall patterns to shrinking ice sheets, rising sea levels, floods and droughts.
 
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide: **
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound made up of molecules that each have **one carbon atom covalently double bonded to two oxygen atoms**.
 
• Atmospheric CO₂ is the** primary carbon source for life on Earth.**
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂ ) is an **important heat-trapping gas, or greenhouse gas.**
 
• CO₂ comes from the extraction and burning of fossil fuels (such as coal, oil, and natural gas), from wildfires, and from natural processes like volcanic eruptions.
